$comment: Feature map read by packages/create-nest-next-auth. Entries with "status": "planned" are not offered by the CLI. Entries with "kind": "hidden" come in through another feature's "requires" instead of being picked directly. Files and env vars listed here are deleted from a generated project when the feature is not selected. A path may sit under a directory another feature claims, as the provider strategies do under oauth-core; what a path may not do is belong to a feature that is still needed once this one is gone. Lines shared code needs only for one feature carry a `// feature:<id>` marker instead; see the CLI README. A target or shared module owns its files and workspaces: they are deleted when it is not part of the plan, and a planned target is never part of one. The Expo app has been built and run on an iOS simulator against the real server; Android has not been built or run. The bare React Native app only bundles, so it stays planned. A target id or shared id is also a marker name: feature:native-core marks lines that any mobile app needs. A database id is one too: feature:postgres marks lines only the PostgreSQL adapter needs and feature:mongodb lines only the MongoDB adapter needs, and the lines of the database that was not chosen are removed. feature:database-choice marks lines that only choose between the two, and no generated project keeps them. A database owns files, docs, env vars, packages, backend scripts, JSON keys and build approvals, all removed when another database is chosen. Its renames, rewrites and envExamples apply when it is the chosen one: a rewrite replaces a literal text in the files it names, and is the way to change a file that is not formatted with prettier.

rewrites.from:
### Backup MongoDB Data

```bash
# Create backup
docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec mongodb mongodump \
  --username admin \
  --password your-password \
  --authenticationDatabase admin \
  --out /backup

# Copy backup from container
docker cp authboiler-mongodb-prod:/backup ./mongodb-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d)
```
rewrites.to:
### Backup PostgreSQL Data

```bash
# Create backup
docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec -T postgres \
  pg_dump --username app --format custom authboiler > ./postgres-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).dump
```

rewrites.from:
### Restore MongoDB Data

```bash
# Copy backup to container
docker cp ./mongodb-backup-20240101 authboiler-mongodb-prod:/restore

# Restore from backup
docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec mongodb mongorestore \
  --username admin \
  --password your-password \
  --authenticationDatabase admin \
  /restore
```
rewrites.to:
### Restore PostgreSQL Data

```bash
# Restore from backup, with the backend stopped
docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec -T postgres \
  pg_restore --username app --dbname authboiler --clean --if-exists < ./postgres-backup-20240101.dump
```

oauth-core.label: OAuth core
oauth-core.description: Provider registry, start and callback routes, account linking, profile sync. Shared by every OAuth provider.

email-password.label: Email and password
email-password.description: Registration with a 6-digit code, login, password reset.

google.label: Google
google.description: Sign in with a Google account.

github.label: GitHub
github.description: Sign in with a GitHub account.

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.description: Sign in with a Facebook account.

magic-link.label: Magic link
magic-link.description: Sign in with a one-time link sent by email. Works on its own or next to email and password.

totp.label: TOTP two-factor
totp.description: Second factor from an authenticator app, on top of password, magic link or OAuth sign-in. Includes single-use recovery codes.

passkeys.label: Passkeys
passkeys.description: WebAuthn sign-in with platform authenticators, and a passkey as an alternative second factor. Works on its own or next to email and password. When TOTP two-factor is also selected, its verify route accepts a passkey.

microsoft.label: Microsoft
microsoft.description: Sign in with a Microsoft account or Entra ID tenant.

apple.label: Apple
apple.description: Sign in with Apple. Needs an HTTPS callback; Apple posts it as a form.

discord.label: Discord
discord.description: Sign in with a Discord account.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.description: Sign in with LinkedIn OIDC. Needs the OpenID Connect product on the app.

gitlab.label: GitLab
gitlab.description: Sign in with GitLab OIDC, hosted or self-managed. One base URL points it at your own instance.

x.label: X
x.description: Sign in with X. OAuth 2.0 with mandatory PKCE; the address needs the users.email scope on the app.

slack.label: Slack
slack.description: Sign in with Slack OIDC. Identities are per workspace.

twitch.label: Twitch
twitch.description: Sign in with Twitch OIDC. The email claim is requested through the claims parameter.

oidc.label: Generic OIDC
oidc.description: Any OpenID Connect issuer, configured from environment variables. Endpoints come from the discovery document at startup.
